texts: The right common carotid artery is the preferred site for arterial cannulation in neonates and infants on ECMO: A.
It is large enough for a cannula in small babies and is reached through a short neck incision, with the venous cannula placed alongside through the right internal jugular vein into the right atrium.
The tip of the arterial cannula lies at the junction of the innominate artery and the aortic arch, not in the ascending aorta.
Reconstruction of the carotid artery after decannulation has not been shown to improve long-term neurologic outcome.
Femoral cannulation is kept for older children and adults, whose femoral vessels are big enough.
In the picture, the cannon goes down the baby's right carrot and stops where it meets the orca's arch.
Memory hook: in a baby, the cannon goes down the right carrot.
